hypotheses.statement: STORAGE_MISMATCH with oracle mode=exact between anvil and pallet-contracts is an oracle artifact, not a semantic bug: pallet-contracts uses hashed storage keys (e.g. 0xff0f2249... instead of slot 0x0) and little-endian value encoding, while raw numeric values are identical after decoding (e.g. EVM 0xff...80 vs polkadot 0x80ff.. both = -128; 0xd4 vs 0xd4 00.. both = 212). Any exact-mode storage comparison across these backends will diverge spuriously.

evidence.note: All 5 STORAGE_MISMATCH entries differ only in key derivation (hashed key vs slot 0) and byte order (LE vs BE); decoded values are numerically identical at every step, including step 4 where both sides are 0xff..ff (-1) yet still flagged due to key mismatch.

hypotheses.next_probe: Re-run the same int-shift-cast-rounding spec with oracle storage mode changed to decoded/normalized (or storage disabled and return values + readLast queries used instead); prediction: verdict becomes PASS.

hypotheses.statement: solang agrees with solc on core signed-int semantics: arithmetic right shift of negatives (-1024 >> 3 = -128), division truncated toward zero (-7 / 2 = -3), signed modulo sign of dividend (-7 % 2 = -1), narrowing cast chains (int16 -300 -> uint8 = 212), and logical shift on bytes4-cast uint32 (0x80000001 >> 1 = 0x40000000). Return values and decoded storage matched on every step.

evidence.note: No RETURN_MISMATCH or REVERT_MISMATCH reported; after decoding the LE storage values, both backends computed -128, -3, -1, 212, and 0x40000000 identically across all steps.

hypotheses.next_probe: Probe edge cases not yet covered: INT64_MIN >> 1, INT64_MIN / -1 (overflow revert behavior), shift by >= bit width, and uint->int casts where the value exceeds the target's max (e.g. int8(uint8(255))); compare return data and revert reasons only.
